summary.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY26 revenue rose 77% YoY to Rs 496 crore, with EBITDA up 305% to Rs 125 crore and margin at 25%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 77% YoY to Rs 496 crore, led by CDMO at Rs 314 crore (+113%) and CRO at Rs 182 crore (+38%). EBITDA rose 305% to Rs 125 crore, with margin at 25%, and PAT turned positive at Rs 60 crore versus a loss of Rs 13 crore a year earlier. Management said CDMO is lumpy, reiterated that H2 has historically been stronger than H1, and stated there were no one-off or launch-stocking items in Q1. Capex of Rs 134 crore was spent in the quarter, with about Rs 700 crore planned for the current year.

financial_highlights.change: Management cited 14% YoY improvement in EBITDA; margin expansion stated as significant
vs loss of Rs 13 crore in Q1 FY25

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 314 crore, up 113% YoY, driven by certain commercial products and early-phase R&D revenue from pharma companies. Management said the business is lumpy and better judged over longer periods.

segments.name: CRO
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 182 crore, up 38% YoY, driven by Integrated Discovery programs. Customer mix in CRO was about 38% big pharma and 62% biotech.

guidance_outlook: Management is not giving specific guidance for FY27 but expects H2 to be stronger than H1, as seen in prior years.
Medium-term: 3-5 year average growth target of 15% for the business; no separate CRO vs CDMO growth numbers given.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 28-30% as revenue scales; Q1 margin of 25% described as a step toward it.
CRO/CDMO revenue mix broadly guided at two-thirds CDMO to one-third CRO, with quarterly deviations possible.
Steady-state CRO margin expected to be a few bps above CDMO margin, per CFO; no split disclosed.
Management said interest cost decline discussed earlier has largely occurred and is reflected in Q1.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity: about 600 KL at end FY25; two new production blocks totalling about 450-550 KL. First block by Q3 FY27, second towards end FY27; manufacturing capacity to rise about 80-90%.
About 91-100 KL brought online at end of Q1 FY26.
Process R&D capacity to nearly double; new Process R&D block started, adding clinical-scale peptide and early-phase formulation capabilities.
About 30% extra Discovery space to be added by fiscal year end; new biology facility launched at Hyderabad campus.
Capex of about Rs 700 crore planned for FY27; further capex expected next year but no figure given.
demand_pricing: Management said RFP flow is healthy, including for mid-stage and late-stage assets.
An existing dedicated CRO client expanded its business by about 30%, effective about a month and a half before the call, expected to flow through from Q2.
Biotech funding is returning but mainly for later-stage CDMO assets; discovery contracts are smaller (20-30 FTE vs 100-150 FTE previously).
Top 10 customers were about 40% of revenue on a full-year basis; company does not disclose quarterly concentration.
Onboarded several new large pharma customers and deepened existing relationships; no specific strategy to favour big pharma over biotech.
Management said India has not yet caught up with China in scale or technology, but China+1 diversification is real, partly due to IP concerns in China.
Management expects R&D to remain in Asia and tariff/reshoring effects on supply geography to be short-term bumps; large pharma does not intend to make advanced intermediates in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be stronger than H1 this year, and is there any lumpiness in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 stronger is a general trend and expected to continue, but no specific FY27 guidance; no one-offs in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is manufacturing capacity doubling by FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Process R&D capacity doubling; manufacturing up about 80-90% (from about 600 KL base, with 450-550 KL being added).

qa_highlights.question: Phase III pipeline count and commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase III pipeline is 10 molecules after net movement; a couple moved to commercial and a couple dropped out. Two Phase III molecules reported positive readouts; one small molecule recently approved.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and capacity timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 77% last quarter; 70-75% considered fully utilised depending on project mix. First new block by Q3 FY27, second towards end FY27; external agencies used in the interim.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 700 crore capex for FY27 only?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, Rs 700 crore is for this year, covering manufacturing, Discovery, process R&D and peptide capabilities; next year will also have capex but no number given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new capacity cause a shift in work, given US reshoring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that US capacity additions mainly involve late-stage and final formulation work; large pharma is not planning to do intermediates in-house, so impact on Indian CDMO work is not seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Growth expectation for the CRO business?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate CRO growth number; committed to 15% average growth over 3-5 years for the business overall. CRO steady-state margin expected to be a few bps above CDMO.

risks_watch: CDMO revenue lumpiness; Q1 CDMO revenue of Rs 314 crore may not be a sustainable base.
Capacity gap until the first new block arrives by Q3 FY27, relying on internal capacity and external agencies.
Phase III pipeline fell in count with two dropouts due to clinical trial failure; further attrition could affect future CDMO revenue.
Client concentration: top 10 customers about 40% of revenue; disclosed annually only.
Geopolitical and US tariff uncertainty on pharma supply geography; management called the impact early and uncertain.
Execution of about Rs 700 crore capex and ramp-up of new blocks, with utilisation targets of 70-80%.
Management did not quantify revenue from newly commercial products, and did not disclose the scientist headcount across CDMO and CRO.
summary.management_tone: Confident and bullish on demand and capacity, with clear caution on CDMO lumpiness and on giving forward numbers. Management avoided quantifying new-product contribution, client-level detail and CRO vs CDMO splits, and said macro/tariff effects are too early to call.
key_quotes: That's just an honest fact, I think.
We definitely have a lot more visibility than when we built in the past, because the past investments also were kind of changing our technology platforms.
I think we are not presenting a separate growth number for CRO versus the CDMO.

adds.what: First new production block (part of 450-550 KL manufacturing addition, ~80-90% capacity rise)
Second new production block (remainder of 450-550 KL manufacturing addition)
Process R&D block (nearly doubling process R&D capacity)
About 30% extra Discovery space at CRO by fiscal year end

growth.why: Management commits to a 3-5 year 15% average growth rate (not FY27-specific) and expects H2 stronger than H1; backing is partial via a first 450-550 KL capacity block due by Q3 FY27 (~80-90% manufacturing capacity rise), a 30% CRO client expansion already effective, and healthy RFP flow, with Rs 700 crore FY27 capex.
